agent_trace.summary: In brain MRI, the image plane is identified by which structures are simultaneously visible and how they are arranged. Seeing both cerebral hemispheres with the lateral ventricles, deep gray matter, and the brainstem in a single slice is most consistent with an axial (transverse) plane. The retrieved SLAKE chunk supports that this is a head/brain MRI context, but it does not determine the plane by itself.

key_facts: Axial brain MRI slices are viewed from top to bottom and commonly show both hemispheres symmetrically.
The lateral ventricles and deep gray matter are often well seen on axial images.
The brainstem can be included on lower axial slices near the base of the brain.
Coronal images show front-to-back anatomy, while sagittal images show side profile structures such as the corpus callosum and brainstem midline.
